title: ATUM-FIB microscopy for targeting and multiscale imaging of rare events in mouse cortex
protocol: Transfer tissue samples into glass vials filled with 2–3 mL 0.1 M cacodylate buffer.
Wash the tissue at least three times with 0.1 M cacodylate buffer.
Replace osmium by filtered 2.5% potassium hexacyanoferrate in 0.1 M cacodylate buffer without additional washing steps.
The tissue is washed at least three times with 0.1 M cacodylate buffer.
Incubate in filtered 1% aqueous TCH.
Wash at least three times with water.
Incubate in 2% aqueous osmium tetroxide.
Wash at least three times with water.
Transfer tissue into a fresh glass vial with 1% uranyl acetate and incubate at 4°C for 15 hours.
Incubate in 1% uranyl acetate at 50°C for 2 hours.
Protect samples from light during the above steps.
Dehydrate tissue in increasing ethanol concentrations (15%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 100%, 100%, 100% ethanol) by exchanges every 10–15 minutes.
Infiltrate tissue in LX112 resin: at least 2 hours at different resin concentrations (acetone mixed with 25%, 50%, 75%, 90% LX112).
Incubate tissue for 15 hours and another 4 hours in freshly prepared 100% LX112.
Prepare LX112 resin: Mix 10 g of LX112 with 6.45 g of DDSA and 4.35 g of NMA, then stir for 10 minutes.
Add 0.3 mL of DMP-30 to the mixture and stir for an additional 20 minutes.
Transfer tissue onto parafilm-coated glass slides.
Fill a plastic capsule with resin and invert it onto the tissue piece.
Cure resin blocks at 60°C for 10 hours until solid and not sticky.
Fix the cured resin block in a sample holder for trimming.
Use a Trim 90 knife to trim 400–800 μm at all 4 sides at a 90°C angle.
Remove resin chips immediately using a deduster.
Incubate the sample holder in the oven at 40°C.
Install the infrared lights left and right of the diamond knife.
Measure the temperature there and adjust it by varying the distance to the knife boat.
Fix the sample holder in the ultramicrotome.
Align the heated diamond knife to the sample block face.
Start sectioning 100–300 nm sections until the full block face appears.
Heat the knife to 40°C.
Install the CNT tape into the Powertome.
Adjust the tension by running jog forward and backward until the target value is 2.7–2.8.
Insert the tape nose into the water bath.
Approach the tape to a distance of approximately 1–1.5 section lengths away from the diamond edge.
Adjust the cutting thickness to 0.5–10 μm.
Start sectioning at 0.1–0.3 mm/s.
Adjust the tape speed to 0.2–0.4 mm/s during cutting and to 0 during retraction.
Guide the section onto the tape with a brush if needed.
Collect serial sections.
Control the proper section uptake by the tape.
Disassemble the tape from the tape collector reel.
Cut tape with sections into 5 cm strips and keep the orientation and order.
Position glass slides on a heating plate (60°C).
Place water drops onto the glass slide.
Position two 5 cm tape strips per slide onto the water drops using forceps.
Do not touch the sections.
Load the series of glass slides into a slide scanner rack.
In the Pannoramic Midi II software load the first slide and manually or automatically label areas covering the tissue sections.
Select sections by thresholding.
Image using the autofocusing and the extended focus level functions (9 focus levels, focus step size 0.2 μm × 5) using the 20× objectives.
Set the autofocus range by testing it for several sections on different slide locations.
Save the protocol for the respective slide.
Repeat step b. for all slides.
Start the automated acquisition of all slides.
Generate jpeg files of the individual sections manually from the original data using Pannoramic software CaseViewer2.2 (3D Histech).
Pause Point: months
Prepare for serial scanning electron microscopy.
Proceed with serial scanning electron microscopy of serial semi-thick sections.
Postcure light microscopy samples on glass slides in an oven for 30–48 h at 60°C.
Prepare a 4-inch silicon wafer by attaching up to three conductive carbon adhesive strips onto it.
Remove the plastic covering the adhesive tapes and keep it.
Detach CNT strips with tissue sections from the glass slide using forceps.
Assemble CNT strips onto the adhesive tape carefully.
Cover the sections with the plastic foil kept from step 39.
Smooth down the sections by hand or using a roller.
Attach 1-2 mm carbon adhesive strips along the sides of the CNT tape.
Connect the CNT tape to the carbon conductive tape and the silicon.
Store the wafer under vacuum or in a dry container until imaging.
Load the wafer into a SEM (Crossbeam Gemini 340, Zeiss).
Acquire serial section images using a backscatter detector (BSD) at 4 keV.
Set the working distance to 7-8 mm and use an aperture of 30 or 60 μm.
Maintain a current of 300 μA during imaging.
Generate a wafer overview map at 1,000 × 1,000 to 3,000 × 3,000 nm in ATLAS 5 Array Tomography.
Map and image sections at medium resolution (60 × 60 to 100 × 100 nm).
Acquire regions of interest from these section sets at 10 × 10 nm with a dwell time of 2 μs and line average of 2.
Align images in TrakEM2 using automated and manual steps, registered and analyzed in Fiji.
Identify target regions based on light and/or electron microscopy data for vasculature, cell somata or other structures ranging from 2 to 10 μm.
Segment and reconstruct selected objects using VAST.
Transfer the section(s) with the structure of interest onto a FIB stub.
Use a scalpel to cut the carbon adhesive around the section of interest on the two sides adjacent to the space between the previous and next section.
Lift the adhesive tape with the section of interest with the scalpel.
Add carbon cement (Science Services) on a FIB stub and position the sample onto it.
Remove remaining carbon cement and let dry for 2 h.
Use silver paint to surround the section helping to ground the sample.
Let the prepared sample dry.
Coat with a thin carbon layer using a sputter coater (e.g., Quorum).
Store the sample under vacuum until the imaging session.
Apply FIB-SEM to generate a high resolution dataset at isotropic voxels.
Segment and render target structures.
Identify the region of interest using BSD imaging.
Sketch schematics for targeted FIB-SEM on a semi-thick section.
Expose tissue cross-section (5 μm) by milling trench.
Cover the region of interest with carbon and platinum.
Capture an InlenseDuo image highlighting myelinated axons and postsynaptic densities.
Segment and render myelinated axons, PSDs, and nuclei.
Load the sample into the SEM.
Image the section using the SE detector at 5–8 kV landing energy and 1.5–2 mm working distance.
Identify the region of interest according to the rough position within the section and suitable landmarks.
Find the eucentric point for FIB-SEM preparation.
Find the coincidence point for FIB-SEM preparation.
Deposit a carbon layer at the site of interest.
Mill a trench with x and y dimensions covering the area of interest and a depth exceeding the sample thickness by 3–5 μm.
Polish the cross-section after milling.
Set up the FIB-SEM run choosing suitable imaging and milling conditions.
Acquire the entire region of interest (typically 10–50 × 10–50 × 6 μm for a 5 μm thick section).
Start with larger section thicknesses (typically 20–50 nm) and readjust to the target z resolution close to the region of interest.
Monitor the FIB-SEM run and adjust parameters if needed.
Align FIB-SEM image stacks in Fiji TrakEM2.
Combine InlenseDuo and SE detector images in the desired ratio.
Segment objects of interest using VAST.
Export segmented objects as .obj files.
Render .obj files using Blender to obtain 3D models and generate movies.
